newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: PLO protests to U.N. over Israeli settlement policy.
newsitem.headline: PLO protests to U.N. over Israeli settlement policy.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation called on the international community on Monday to take a "clear and firm position" against Israel's settlement policy.

In a letter to Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, the PLO's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, said: "The government of Israel has resumed the drive of settler colonialism in the occupied Palestinian territory, including Jerusalem, which represents an extremely dangerous development."

He cited the recent removal of restrictions placed on settlement activities by the previous Israeli government and the approval of plans for placing mobile homes in some settlements and for building housing units in others.
"Those settlement activities contradict international humanitarian law and many resolutions of United Nations organs, including the Security Council," al-Kidwa said.
"They also violate the agreements between the government of Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation and could reverse the peace process as a whole," he wrote.
He said there were "about 170 colonial settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory with approximately 300,000 Israeli settlers," about half of them in the East Jerusalem area.

"This has all been done through the brutal confiscation of land, the seizure of water and other natural resources and the harassment and the terrorisation of the Palestinian people by armed settlers, and it has led to the dismemberment of the Palestinian land," he continued.

Al-Kidwa said he expected the international community to "take a clear and firm position, based on international law and in line with previous United Nations resolutions, against Israel's settlement policy and practices."
